title: Data Center Facility Manager, Data Center Community
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical technical leader who ensures the heartbeat of our global infrastructure remains strong and resilient. In this pivotal role, you'll be the guardian of our data center operations, driving reliability and performance while optimizing operational efficiency across complex technical environments.

Data Center Facility Manger role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including electrical support equipment such as stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems that include but not limited to switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAC units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire suppression systems, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.


Key job responsibilities
- Oversee all aspects of the data center's critical infrastructure. Ensure that all work performed within the space is done to high quality and without impact to internal/external customers
- Oversee the safety, security, availability, quality, and performance of the team, while driving a positive customer experience across multiple shift schedules
- Manage teams of 24x7 engineering technicians and Facility Managers in all facets of their career
- Engage in improvement projects, often requiring reaching out to a variety of support teams, and drive them from conception to completion
- Ensure staffing levels are maintained and grow with expansions
- Be actively involved in ongoing construction activities
- Coordinate daily with a multitude of third-party vendors ensuring adherence to contracted SLAs
- Effectively and efficiently manage the operations budget and expenditures

A day in the life
As the Facility Manager, your role demonstrates a strong commitment to prioritizing the development and well-being of team members, as well as fostering diversity and inclusion. You will oversee all facets of the data center's critical infrastructure with a focus on continuous availability and optimal performance, while upholding high-quality standards and minimizing any impact on internal and external customers. Additionally, you will play a crucial role in process optimization, staff management, setting performance metrics, and driving continuous improvement initiatives, all while ensuring a supportive and inclusive work environment.

- Manage teams of 24x7 engineering technicians: Prioritize and assign tasks, coach and create documentation, guide and train staff on best practices.
- Effectively and efficiently manage operations budget: Monitor and control expenditures, ensure optimal resource allocation.
- Engage in improvement projects: Drive projects from conception to completion, collaborate with support teams.
- Coordinate with third-party vendors: Ensure adherence to contracted service level agreements (SLAs).
- Communicate complex technical information: Adapt communication style for diverse stakeholders, including non-technical audiences.
- Respond to out-of-hours emergency calls: Address urgent issues that may arise outside regular working hours.
- Act as an escalation point for facilities-related issues: Oversee routine and emergency services, ensure safety procedures are followed.
- Deliver operational excellence: Prioritize team development and well-being while achieving operational goals.
- Foster a diverse and inclusive team culture: Empower team members to reach their full potential.
- Perform physical tasks: Lift and move objects of varying weights, walk job sites in different terrains while maintaining balance and safety.
- Promote accessible work environments: Support employees' diverse needs.
- Work in noisy environments when required: Utilize approved personal protective equipment (PPE).
- Support multiple locations/sites: Coordinate and manage operations across different sites.
- Provide on-site management for builders, five days a week. (No remote work)

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- 3+ years of in industrial electrical or mechanical systems experience
- 5+ years of work in a managerial/supervisory with 8-10 or more direct reports

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of the electrical and mechanical systems involved in critical data center operations including systems such as feeders, transformers, generators, switchgear, UPS systems, ATS units, PDU units, chillers, pumps, air handling units, and CRAC units
- Experience communicating technical details verbally and in writing

descriptionHtml:
Amazonでは、障がいを持つ社員がそれぞれ自分の能力を活かし、様々な部門で活躍しています。社内外の関係者が連携しながら、ひとりひとりの障がいに合わせた必要なサポートを提供します。
アマゾンジャパンのフルフィルメントセンター（物流拠点）における、メンテナンスチーム業務のサポートを担当していただきます。

メンテナンスチームの主な業務は以下の通りです。
１．設備・装置の安定稼働のサポートとメンテナンス。
２．故障した設備・装置の修理・復旧。
３．故障原因を調査し、再発防止対策を策定。
４．装置の性能・生産性の改善策を策定・実施。

このうち、メンテナンス業務をサポートする部品の発注・納品管理、検品・検収、在庫管理、データ集計などのデスクワークを中心に行っていただきます。

３．納品された品物の検品、検収、移動、入庫処理。
４．メンテナンスチームから依頼されたデータ集計などパソコンでの⼊⼒。

title: Logistics Specialist, Data Center - 2027 Internship
descriptionHtml:
Important — Site Location & Commuting: This role is based at a data center facility in a remote location with no public transportation access. A valid driving license and access to personal transportation are required to commute to the site daily. Please consider this before applying.

Behind every click, stream, and cloud service is real hardware — and someone needs to make sure it gets where it needs to be. As a Logistics Specialist Intern at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will help manage the supply chain that keeps our data centers running, from receiving and tracking parts to ensuring the right equipment is in the right place at the right time.

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Logistics Specialist position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:
- Students in the last year of their Technical/Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Supply Chain, Logistics, or a similar discipline who are looking for an internship that could lead to a full-time career.

About the Role

You will join a creative, dynamic team of Logistics Specialists dedicated to providing world-class customer service — and you will be part of operating the world's largest cloud computing infrastructure. This hands-on role supports our procurement and supply chain operations. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do
- Monitor inventory levels to ensure proper stock levels are maintained
- Receive parts, maintain inventory records, and check out parts
- Load and unload shipments and transport parts between different locations
- Assemble, address, stamp, and arrange for the shipment of merchandise and materials
- Assist in daily scheduling of deliveries and pick-ups to and from production locations Unpack incoming shipments and verify contents
- Maintain precise records of all commodities going in and out of the facility
- Physical Requirements
- This role involves physical activity, including:
- Regularly lifting and moving up to 16 kilograms (approximately 35 pounds) unassisted, and participating in group lifts for heavier items
- Lifting loads of up to 22 kilograms (approximately 49 pounds) and carrying them for short distances
- Continuously climbing and descending stairs safely (applies to sites with stairs)
- Reaching and stretching to position equipment and fixtures while maintaining balance
- Pushing or pulling heavy objects into position
- If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation during the application or hiring process, visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information.

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 consecutive weeks, starting in summer 2027. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday through Friday.

This is a paid internship.

Please note that a full-time Logistics Specialist position could involve day, evening, or weekend shifts and on-call rotations. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position.

- Action. You will move fast, solve real logistics challenges, and see the results of your work every day. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice.
- Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will learn how a world-class supply chain operates at massive scale and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.
- Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Our team is dedicated to supporting new members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skill set. Your journey here is yours to shape.

title: 2027 Business Developer Intern, Amazon Payments
descriptionHtml:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact. You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless pportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?


What’s in it for you?

An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Key job responsibilities
Amazon is looking for ambitious, curious and versatile individuals to join our unique world as interns. Our Amazon internship will provide you with an exceptional opportunity to experience a fast-paced, dynamic and internationally diverse environment; it will boost your resume, and provide a superb introduction to our daily responsibilities. We are looking for a highly driven, entrepreneurial, analytical and customer-obsessed Business Developer Intern. You are the ideal candidate if:

- You are excited by contributing to launching and help developing a new business

- You are able to help manage the relationship with partners and prospects, and meet and exceed program goals.

- You are able to translate customer needs into product requirements

title: Program Manager, II
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring a Program Manager to own the first line of defense (1LoD) Buyer Compliance controls for the Amazon Business (AB) Gift Card (GC) cohort of customers. This role will provide regional support for either Singapore (SG)/Japan (JP), Mexico (MX), or Europe (EU). The Program Manager will be accountable for managing risk directly by collaborating with Risk Specialists to perform customer due diligence, Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification, Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM) investigations, and enforcement actions, and by collaborating with the second line of defense (2LoD) on regulatory filing across their respective regions. The Program Manager will own the day-to-day controls and is the single-threaded owner for compliance outcomes in their regions.

Key job responsibilities
Define and maintain the operating cadence, SLAs, and quality bar for KYC and SAM within the assigned region.

Establish and drive mechanisms to measure and improve control effectiveness, working across Compliance Officers, Machine Learning Scientists, and Engineering teams to refine and continuously improve evaluations.

Collaborate with Risk Specialist Operations teams to investigate alerts and escalations, document findings, and determine filing requirements in parallel with 2LoD.

Partner with 2LoD regional compliance, legal, product, operations, and compliance officers to represent regional compliance status in business and risk reviews.

Own regional compliance metrics and reporting, surfacing risk trends and gaps with recommended remediation actions.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
- Bachelor's degree
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements
- Experience across the domain of risk management & compliance operations

title: Risk Analyst II, Account Integrity
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Account Integrity Team (AIT) within Buyer Risk Prevention (BRP) protects hundreds of millions of customers by identifying and stopping fraudulent activity before it causes harm. The Risk Mining function is where human ingenuity meets machine learning - our team detects emerging modus operandi (MOs) that automated systems alone can't catch, and feeds those signals back into scalable upstream defenses. Nowhere is that fight sharper than in Anti-Automation, where we go head-to-head with bots, scripted attacks, and automated abuse that evolves by the hour. If you want to do investigative work that directly translates into customer trust at global scale, this is the role.

The Risk Analyst II (Risk Mining) is a senior individual-contributor role that sits at the intersection of three disciplines - analyst, strategist, and ML partner. You will join the Anti-Automation Risk Mining team in India - a team of analysts, investigators, and builders who hunt down automated abuse before it scales. As the analyst, you run deep dives on bot and scripted-attack behavior and turn raw signal into high-quality MO documentation. As the strategist, you shape where the vertical invests its detection effort and anticipate how the adversary will evolve. As the ML partner, you work hand-in-hand with Machine Learning and Engineering to convert your findings into scalable, automated upstream defenses and close the feedback loop into models and rules.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role with broad cross-team influence, reporting to Risk Mining leadership. You are accountable for the quality, speed, and impact of your investigations - detecting automated MOs, driving measurable gains in detection speed and precision, mitigating risk, and clearing the blockers that stand between the team and impact. As a senior IC, you are expected to raise the bar for investigation quality across the vertical and influence detection strategy well beyond your own caseload.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead complex investigations into emerging automated abuse - running deep dives on bots, scripted attacks, and automated MOs before they scale, and setting the quality bar others follow.
- Own detection and mitigation strategy for the Anti-Automation vertical - prioritizing the highest-risk automated MOs and anticipating how bots and scripted attacks will evolve.
- Partner deeply with Machine Learning and Engineering teams to turn your findings into scalable, automated upstream defenses, and own the feedback loop back into models and rules.
- Translate investigative signal into ML features, detection logic, and rule improvements - acting as the bridge between front-line investigation and automated defense.
- Produce high-quality deep dives, MO write-ups, and analyses, and own vertical-level metrics for detection volume, speed, and precision.
- Collaborate with the other Risk Mining verticals and partner teams (Payment Risk, Abuse Risk Mining) on joint investigations and shared signals.
- Serve as a subject-matter expert on high-severity incidents and escalations.
- Champion automation and GenAI opportunities to amplify throughput and quality, and measure the realized ROI from those investments.

A day in the life
No two days look the same when the automated-abuse landscape shifts in real time - your week balances hands-on investigation, strategy, and close ML partnership to keep Anti-Automation ahead of emerging threats:

Analyst (Investigation & Analysis)
- Running deep dives on the highest-risk automated MOs and following the signal in the noise and take mitigation action.
- Pulling and analyzing large datasets to size impact, confirm hypotheses, and sharpen detection.
- Documenting findings and MO write-ups so they can be turned into durable, scalable defenses.

Strategy (Building What's Next)
- Shaping the detection and mitigation strategy for your slice of Risk Mining - anticipating how automated abuse will evolve and positioning the team to stay ahead.
- Championing GenAI and automation opportunities as a core part of the vertical's strategy.

ML Partnership (Scaling the Defense)
- Partnering with ML and Engineering to turn your findings into automated defenses that scale.
- Translating investigative signal into features, detection logic, and rule improvements.
- Owning the feedback loop so model and rule performance keeps improving on the MOs you surface.

Tactical (Keeping the Engine Running)
- Reporting detection metrics and progress on key goals.
- Responding to live escalations when a new automated attack surfaces.

About the team
The Risk Mining team within Account Integrity spans India, US, and Costa Rica, and works for Amazon's worldwide marketplace to detect and disrupt bad-actor behavior.

Our mission is simple: find the signal in the noise before bad actors cause harm. We operate across three risk verticals - Anti-Automation, Account Takeover, and Bad Actor Account - and partner closely with Machine Learning, Engineering, and Product teams to turn our investigative findings into scalable upstream defenses. The Anti-Automation vertical sits at the front line of that fight, taking on bots and scripted abuse at the scale.

If you want to do work where your findings directly translate into customer trust at global scale - and where the adversary never stops evolving - this is the team.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience with advanced use of SQL for data mining and business intelligence, or experience with data analytics platforms (Power BI, Python, SQL, Tableau)
- Experience delivering results for large, cross-functional initiatives/projects
- 5+ years of experience in an analytics or data-driven role (e.g. business analyst, risk analyst, data analyst, operations analyst, or research analyst) or similar quantitative/analytical roles across any domain

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of program requirements definition and data and metrics leveraging to drive improvements experience
- Experience handling confidential information

title: SDE II, EE Experiences, Progressive Discovery and Monetization
descriptionHtml:
Everyday Essentials (EE) is a $100B+ business and one of the fastest-growing categories at Amazon — the household staples, health and personal care, grocery, and beauty products hundreds of millions of customers reorder. We're reinventing how customers discover, buy, and get more value from them, and we're looking for Software Development Engineers who want to build that future.

The EE Experiences organization builds the shopping experience for the products customers come back for most. Our charter is Progressive Discovery and Monetization: helping customers find better products for their needs, complete their baskets, and improve EE business economics — and giving the world's largest consumer brands new and effective ways to reach those customers and grow with Amazon. We build a durable, profitable business at the intersection of the two, on the surfaces customers use every day.

This is a space where the hardest problems don't have off-the-shelf answers. We're not polishing a solved product — we're inventing experiences that don't exist yet, and the decisions we make now shape a business with room to grow for years. You'll build discovery and recommendation features, brand-facing advertising surfaces, and the backend services that power them. Your work moves from whiteboard to production in front of a very large customer base, with visibility all the way to senior leadership.

We're an AI-first team, and that shows up in two ways. We use AI throughout how we build software, and we expect our engineers to keep learning and applying the latest tools to move faster and raise the quality bar. AI is also at the core of what we build — the intelligence that helps customers find the right product is a modeling and engineering problem we work on hand in hand with scientists. If you're curious about AI, learn quickly, and like using it to solve real customer problems while keeping a clear head about where it helps and where it doesn't, you'll fit right in.

Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and own software end to end — from customer research through design, code, testing, deployment, and production operations.
Take on ambiguous problems where the goal is clear but the path is not, bring clarity, and deliver simple solutions that improve how customers find and buy everyday essentials.
Partner closely with scientists, product managers, and designers to turn customer and brand problems into products that ship worldwide.
Use generative AI tools and modern engineering practices to raise quality and velocity, and coach teammates on getting the most from them.
Own operational health for your services — monitor metrics, drive root-cause fixes, and keep improving the experience for customers and brand partners.
Raise the technical bar through code reviews, mentoring, and hiring for the best talent.

A day in the life
Most days start with the customer problem in front of you: how to help someone find better everyday-essentials products faster, or how to give brands a more effective way to reach shoppers or how to improve the profitability of the business. You dig into data, sketch a design, and talk it through with product managers and scientists before writing any code. By the afternoon you might be prototyping an idea that didn't exist yesterday, reviewing a teammate's change, or debugging something in production. Because so much here is new, you won't just pick up tickets. You'll help decide what to build, push for the approach you believe in, and see your work reach customers in weeks, not quarters.

About the team
Our team owns how customers discover and buy the everyday essentials they rely on — and how the brands behind those products reach them. Our mission is to make restocking the things you need effortless, help customers find better options and to improve the business economics along the way. Day to day you'll work with fellow engineers and partner closely with product managers, designers, and scientists, who bring the customer and data insight that shapes what we build. We're a small, fast-moving group solving open-ended problems for hundreds of millions of shoppers — a place where you own problems end to end and your ideas reach customers fast.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers
- Experience debugging, profiling, and implementing best software engineering practices in large-scale systems

- Students in the last year of their Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field who are looking for an internship that could lead to a full-time career.

About the Role

As an intern, you will provide technical support within Amazon's owned and operated data centers. Your work will ensure that the data center's mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems operate at 100% availability while maintaining first-class customer service to the teams and groups on site.

You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do

The Engineering Operations team is Amazon's front-line responders for hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. You will work with equipment that supports mission-critical servers and must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. This equipment includes, but is not limited to:

- Stand-by diesel generators and switchgear
- Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPSs) and Power Distribution Units (PDUs)
- Air Handling Units (AHUs), chillers, and cooling towers
- Chemical treatment systems, pumps, motors, and Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)
- Building automation systems

Your day-to-day duties include:
- Maintaining mechanical and electrical equipment
- Assisting with root cause analysis of equipment failures
- Troubleshooting facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
- Taking daily operational readings of all mechanical and electrical equipment
- Using internal Computerized Maintenance
- Management Systems (CMMS) to manage building workflows
- Interacting with third-party vendors and contractors working on site

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 consecutive weeks. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday through Friday.

Please note that full-time Engineering Operations Technician roles operate on a rotating shift pattern, which may include days, nights, weekends, and public holidays. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying.

Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity

At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go.

From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will troubleshoot and maintain the systems that keep AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at massive scale.

- Impact. Your work shapes the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. From cloud computing to artificial intelligence, the systems you maintain power it all.
- Action. You will move fast, experiment, and learn by doing. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice.
- Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will apply what you learned in the classroom to real challenges and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.
- Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Beyond that, you will find continuous learning opportunities and the chance to work on different projects. Your journey here is yours to shape.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on.
You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers.

title: Mechanical Engineer - Thermal Analysis, Amazon Prime Air, Drone Delivery
descriptionHtml:
Hardware Development Engineer II – Thermal Analysis

We are seeking a Hardware Development Engineer II to join our Electric Propulsion Subsystem team. In this role, you will be a significant and autonomous contributor, solving difficult thermal engineering problems for an electric aerial drone. You will own the thermal analysis and thermal management strategy for the vehicle's battery pack, electric motors, power electronics, and avionics, developing high-fidelity FEA and CFD models that drive design decisions.

This position requires an engineer who demonstrates strong technical depth in heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and numerical simulation while also exhibiting the system-level thinking and influence characteristic of our most impactful contributors.



Key job responsibilities
• Develop high-fidelity FEA and CFD thermal models of the drone's battery pack, motors, power electronics, and avionics, capturing conduction, convection, and radiation across the full flight envelope and ambient operating range.
• Define and develop thermal management strategies and systems for the battery pack, including cold-weather heating, in-flight and ground cooling, and cell-to-cell temperature uniformity.
• Develop cooling strategies for electric motors and motor controllers, including forced-air and conductive paths, and trade thermal performance against mass, drag, and packaging constraints.
• Analyze candidate designs and quantify thermal margins, hot-spot locations, transient temperature response, and sensitivity to operating conditions, and communicate results as clear design recommendations.
• Perform thermal analysis of avionics systems, defining heat-sinking, airflow, and conduction paths that maintain component junction temperatures within reliability limits.
• Build reduced-order and lumped-parameter thermal models derived from high-fidelity simulations for use in system-level performance, range, and mission-planning tools.
• Define and execute thermal test campaigns, including instrumented bench tests, environmental chamber tests, and flight test data collection, and correlate physical results to analysis models.
• Establish thermal design requirements and operating limits.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of working in mechanical engineering or equivalent experience
- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or equivalent
- Experience developing and validating thermal models including reduced-order models, FEA, and CFD.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in mechanical engineering or equivalent
- Experience with electric powertrain components and thermal management systems design
- Experience with applicable aerospace design standards including DO-25, DO-160G, SAE AIR1168, or MIL-STD-810

locations: East Palo Alto, CA, United States
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring Principal, Senior, and Distinguished Engineers to join AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services.


AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services is redefining how the world stores, serves, and reasons over data in the age of AI. Our vision is to make every byte of enterprise data instantly durable, infinitely scalable, and intelligent by default — so that organizations of any size can turn their data into insight and action. We pair decades of hard-won operational experience with relentless curiosity to build the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on: object storage (Amazon S3), block storage (Amazon EBS), archival storage (Amazon S3 Glacier), analytics and database engines (Amazon Redshift, EMR, SageMaker), and the ultra-high-performance caching layers that make generative AI and analytics fast and trustworthy at enterprise scale. We're hiring Principal and Senior Principal Engineers across the org to own technical direction for some of our hardest problems: building a new cache product purpose-built for GenAI and analytics — delivering ultra-low-latency, ultra-high-throughput access to S3 data at exponential scale; setting architecture for S3 storage at the exabyte tier; and driving the engineering direction of SageMaker, Redshift, EMR, and AWS Database Services. These are deep, high-ownership systems roles — some remote-eligible, others anchored to hubs like Seattle, Irvine, and Berlin — for engineers who have led org-wide technical strategy and want to see it run in production. If you want to build systems that operate at planet scale — where durability, availability, latency, and failure-mode ownership are first-class concerns measured in eleven nines — this is the team.

What You'll Do

This is a rare chance to own and ship the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on — not features on top of a platform, but the storage, data, and caching layers that everything else depends on, operating at a scale no one else in the industry touches. You'll architect systems that store and serve exabytes of the world's most critical data, where a single design decision ripples across hundreds of millions of customers and millions of applications.

The problems here are unlike anywhere else. How do you deliver eleven nines of durability while adding net-new capabilities to a service that already stores hundreds of trillions of objects? How do you build a new cache product that serves S3 data at ultra-low latency and ultra-high throughput for GenAI and analytics workloads growing exponentially? How do you evolve block, object, and archival storage — and the analytics and database engines on top of them — without ever compromising the durability, availability, and latency guarantees customers have bet their businesses on? These are deep systems challenges solved in production, at a scale where the usual playbooks break down. You help write the new ones.

The systems you build here don't sit in a backlog — they're load-bearing for the internet: S3, EBS, and Glacier storing the data behind modern AI and analytics; Redshift, EMR, and SageMaker turning that data into insight; and the next generation of high-performance caching making all of it fast. You'll have direct influence over technical choices, minimal layers between you and decisions, and the opportunity to define what foundational data infrastructure looks like in the AI era.

title: Technical Program Manager III, Amazon Leo Partner Services (ALPS)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access. With 38 signed distribution partners globally and service launch approaching, now is an exciting time to join a team that is actively shaping how satellite broadband reaches the world.

As a Technical Program Manager on the Amazon Leo Partner Services team, you will own and drive complex, externally facing technical integration programs with Amazon Leo's global distribution partners, including some of the largest internet service providers in the world. You will serve as the primary program leader responsible for ensuring partners successfully integrate, validate, and launch satellite internet service in their contracted territories and channels. This role sits at the center of partner-facing execution and internal product coordination, spanning API onboarding, BSS/OSS integration, network readiness, operational enablement, and launch milestones. You will work cross-functionally with Amazon Leo engineering, product, solutions architecture, and operations teams to ensure partner-facing deliverables are defined, prioritized, and delivered on time.

This position may require access to export-controlled information (ECI) subject to EAR and ITAR. Final employment decision is contingent upon satisfactory completion of export control screenings and obtaining any necessary export licenses or approvals, based on nationality, citizenship, and other factors considered by applicable export control regulations.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end partner technical integration programs from discovery through launch readiness, defining integration scope, success criteria, milestones, and deliverables across partner and Amazon Leo teams while identifying risks, dependencies, and critical path items early to drive mitigation plans.
- Lead recurring program reviews, executive checkpoints, and milestone tracking sessions with strategic distribution partners, translating partner integration requirements into clear internal execution plans and managing blockers through timely escalation.
- Coordinate delivery across multiple internal workstreams — including API releases, backend services, hardware readiness, and operational tooling — partnering with Product, Engineering, Solutions Architects, and Operations teams to align roadmaps with partner launch commitments.
- Develop and maintain standardized program artifacts such as integration plans, dependency maps, and executive status reporting, and implement repeatable frameworks for global partner onboarding and launch readiness.
- Analyze program data, track integration maturity metrics, and report launch risk to senior leadership, using insights to drive continuous improvement of the ALPS launch model and influence prioritization of partner-critical capabilities.

A day in the life
You will operate in a regional context, supporting distribution partners across your assigned region in coordination with central ALPS teammates and other regional Technical Program Managers. Your day may include leading a partner integration review in the morning, aligning with engineering on API readiness in the afternoon, and preparing an executive launch risk update for leadership. Beyond your regional portfolio, you will also own at least one global-scope initiative aimed at improving the partner experience across all ALPS regions, giving you visibility and impact well beyond your immediate territory.

About the team
The Amazon Leo Partner Services (ALPS) team is responsible for the onboarding, integration, and enablement of Amazon Leo's distribution partners worldwide. We work with telecom operators and regional service providers to deliver satellite internet service in inclusive regulatory and operational environments. With a rapidly growing partner network and service launch on the horizon, the team is scaling quickly to meet demand from some of the largest internet service providers in the world.

Our mission is to make Amazon Leo partnerships predictable, scalable, and launch-ready through technical rigor and disciplined program execution. Every team member owns a regional partner portfolio while also driving at least one global project that raises the bar on the partner experience across all markets. This combination of regional depth and global reach means you will build expertise in local market dynamics while shaping how ALPS operates at scale.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 3+ years of software development experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

This role will be physically based at our new MDD Pecos, TX site.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.



A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 4+ years of military experience

title: Principal PM-T, Growth, Outbound Communications
descriptionHtml:
Every day, hundreds of Amazon teams across Retail, Prime, Prime Video, Music, Alexa, and more reach customers through email, push, SMS, and messaging apps. Outbound Communications runs that marketplace, at the scale of hundreds of millions of customers and billions of messages, through everyday sending and Amazon's largest events: Prime Day, Prime Big Deal Days, and the holidays. Each message competes for finite customer attention. The marketplace grows when every message earns more of it: more customers open, click, and buy, and fewer opt out.

We're looking for a Principal Product Manager - Technical to lead growth for this marketplace. You'll own click-through rate, conversion, and incremental sales per message across channels, and the technical products that move them: personalization and recommendations in messages, send-time and channel optimization, new creative and interactive experiences, conversational and messaging channels, and the experimentation engine that tells us what works.

You'll work backwards from the customer. You'll find where messages fail to earn engagement, form hypotheses, and run a high-velocity experimentation program with engineering and science. You'll ship the winners as platform capabilities that every sending team can use, not one-off campaign tweaks. You'll measure growth honestly, on clicks, conversions, incremental OPS, and long-term customer value, not opens, and you'll balance short-term lift against opt-outs and customer trust.



Key job responsibilities
- Own the growth strategy, roadmap, and goals for Outbound's customer attention marketplace: CTR, conversion, incremental OPS per message, and engagement across email, push, SMS, and messaging channels.
- Build and run a high-velocity experimentation program. Set the hypothesis backlog, prioritize by expected impact, and make A/B and multi-armed testing fast, trustworthy, and self-service for every sending team.
- Own the technical products that drive engagement: personalization and recommendations inside messages, send-time and channel selection, content and creative optimization, and interactive and conversational experiences that let customers act without leaving the message.
- Partner with science and engineering to bring ML and AI into who receives what, when, and on which channel, including ranking, propensity and uplift models, bandits, and generative content, and measure their incrementality against holdouts.
- Define the growth funnel and its instrumentation end to end, from delivered to opened, clicked, converted, and retained. Make the data reconcilable, real-time where it matters, and attributable to the module, content, and decision that drove it.
- Grow the addressable audience: opt-in and permission growth for new channels, reactivation of lapsed customers, and deliverability and reach improvements.
- Turn winning experiments into platform capabilities. Write PR/FAQs and requirements, make build-vs-buy and architecture trade-offs with engineering leaders, and drive adoption across partner teams.
- Set growth tenets and guardrails, such as opt-out, complaint, and frequency limits, so growth never comes at the cost of customer trust.
- Influence senior leaders across Retail, Prime, and partner businesses with data and written narratives, and report growth results and learnings in the Outbound business reviews.
- Raise the bar for growth and experimentation practice across Outbound, and mentor product managers.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience technical product management
- 10+ years of technical product or program management experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in project management methodologies, business analysis, or process improvement
- Usage of generative AI tools to enhance workflow efficiency, with a willingness to learn effective prompting and evaluation practices
- Ability to recognize opportunities where generative AI could enhance products, workflows, or customer experiences

title: Senior Design Manager, Supply Chain Facilities Management (SCFM), Supply Chain Facilities Management (SCFM)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Senior Design Manager to join its Supply Chain Facilities Management (SCFM) team Dallas Texas.

Key job responsibilities
Our team is responsible for delivering and sustaining the network of supply chain facilities — warehouses, logistics and distribution hubs, integration and staging centres — that underpin the AWS infrastructure build programme. We drive to develop a portfolio of facilities that emphasise security, safety, efficiency, and cost effectiveness, while finding new ways to keep pace with AWS’s growing demand.
As Global Design Manager in SCFM at AWS, you will own the end-to-end design strategy for supply chain facilities across NALA, EMEA, and APAC — defining technical standards, driving design reviews, and ensuring consistency and quality across the global portfolio.. You will be part of a highly creative and efficient team comprised of Architects, Engineers, and Designers tasked with solving problems and challenging the status quo — across new-build, fit-out, extension, and the technical assessment and repurposing of existing buildings.
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on — and the supply chain and facilities network that makes that delivery possible. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
Key Job Responsibilities
• Communicate conceptual designs and create/maintain project documentation before, during, and after construction and fit-out;
• Lead the technical due diligence of candidate buildings and sites — assessing structural capacity, M&E systems, fire and life safety, compliance, and overall suitability — to inform acquisition, lease, and repurposing decisions;
• Creating and tracking metrics related to cost, quality and duration of design, as well as collecting data from construction and commissioning teams as designs are implemented. Establishing capital project design budgets and contributing to complex business cases for existing region and new region deployment. Collaborating with AWS finance teams to secure funding for projects;
• Working in partnership with AWS Engineering leads to schedule engineering resources and influence design changes based on internal customer needs;
• Partnering with internal customers to establish project scope, schedule and deliverables. Create, review, and release design RFPs. Direct the technical output of external design consultants through the design and construction lifecycle — setting expectations, reviewing deliverables, and ensuring alignment with AWS standards and project requirements. Coordinate with internal and external Mechanical, Electrical, Controls, and Cabling design engineers;
• Think outside of the box to find innovative solutions prior to and during the construction process to reduce costs and schedule without negative impacts on quality or reliability. Travel for site assessments, due diligence surveys, internal design meetings, construction review, and interfacing with design consultants. Anticipated travel not to exceed 25%;
• Coordinate and oversee permitting and design consultant workstreams, ensuring regulatory compliance, schedule adherence, and quality standards are met across concurrent projects.
• Complete after-action reviews and identify opportunities for process improvement.


A day in the life
As a Senior Design Manager you will be a key technical contributor within a global engineering team, partnering with leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver supply chain and capacity projects across the Europe, Middle East & Africa geography. This role is an opportunity to collaborate with many facets of the AWS organization, external engineering resources, and regulatory agencies — spanning new facilities, fit-outs, extensions, and the due diligence and technical assessment of existing buildings being brought into the network.

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Inclusive Team Culture

title: Systems Development Engineer, Lab Operations Platform, Amazon Leo DevOps
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Satellite development moves fast, and the labs that support it never have enough hands for every request. The Amazon Leo Development Operations (DevOps) team runs the labs where spacecraft hardware is built, tested, and qualified, and the right call on any given day depends on knowing exactly what work is waiting, who can do it, and which equipment is ready. Today that picture is assembled by hand. We are looking for a Systems Development Engineer to build the systems that replace it.

You will own the software that connects our lab personnel, lab spaces, and lab equipment, and you will turn scattered scheduling, ticketing, and equipment data into clear, trusted views of capacity and demand. Our lab engineers and technicians are not software developers, so what you build has to be intuitive enough that they want to use it. Over time, the same tools will show which equipment is available and ready, so planning covers people, spaces, and equipment together. Your work will help lab leadership make faster priority calls and keep our design-team customers supported on the most urgent, actionable work.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities

title: Electronics Manufacturing Manager, Amazon Center for Quantum Computing
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Center for Quantum Computing is seeking a Production Manager to lead the medium-volume production of control electronics systems for our experimental quantum computing platforms. Operating at a scale of hundreds of units per year, you will own the end-to-end production process for chassis-level and board-level electronics assemblies — from intake of engineering designs through assembly, test, and delivery to internal customers. You will manage and develop a small team of assembly and test technicians, setting the quality standards, work instructions, and processes that ensure consistent, reliable output. Beyond production execution, you will own the production laboratory space itself, including inventory management and the physical organization and standards of the facility. You will also co-manage the product lifecycle management (PLM) system alongside adjacent hardware engineering and business teams, ensuring alignment across design, production, and program management. The ideal candidate brings a proven track record in electronics production at similar volumes, a hands-on understanding of what it takes to build and test complex electronic assemblies repeatably, and the leadership skills to build a high-performing production team from the ground up.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end production of control electronics assemblies (chassis builds, board-level assemblies, cable harnesses) at medium volume, managing the full lifecycle from procurement through assembly, test, and delivery.
- Lead production scheduling and capacity planning, managing trade-offs between product mix, technician utilization, and delivery commitments.
- Manage and develop a team of assembly and test technicians, setting standards, building a culture of quality and accountability, and serving as a technical escalation resource.
- Own the production laboratory space, including equipment, tooling, inventory, and environmental controls; co-manage the PLM system with adjacent hardware engineering and business teams.
- Partner with hardware engineering to provide DFM and DFT feedback on new designs, and lead root cause analysis and corrective action for production defects and quality escapes.
- Manage supply chain relationships, proactively identifying and mitigating component availability risks and lead-time issues.
- Drive continuous improvement through lean principles and process optimization; work with engineering and senior management to develop and execute production roadmaps aligned with the team's scaling plans.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a technician standup, then a supply chain issue — a connector slipped its delivery date — that you work through with procurement. Mid-morning you walk the floor, inspecting work in progress. After lunch you flag a component placement problem in a new board design before it reaches production. Later you draft a work instruction update for a chassis assembly that keeps generating rework. You close the day in a roadmap review with senior management, presenting capacity forecasts and the infrastructure investments needed to hit next quarter's scaling targets.

About the team
You will join SIGNALS, a multidisciplinary team responsible for all electronics and signal delivery solutions in Amazon's quantum computing systems — spanning from the programmable logic software layer down to microwave signal delivery at the quantum processor package. The team brings together software, electrical, RF, and mechanical engineers solving tightly coupled problems across the full signal chain. As Production Manager, you will be the critical link between engineering design and production reality, ensuring the team's innovations are built reliably and delivered on schedule.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of experience in electronics production, manufacturing, or test engineering.
- Hands-on experience with chassis-level and board-level electronics assembly processes.
- 2+ years of experience managing or supervising technicians or production staff.
- Working knowledge of inventory management and PLM, MRP, or ERP systems.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement production standards, work instructions, and quality processes.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in engineering, manufacturing, or operations management.
- Experience with medium-volume, high-mix production environments (hundreds to low thousands of units per year).
- Familiarity with IPC standards for electronics assembly and workmanship.
- Experience managing supply chains for custom or low-volume electronic assemblies, including component obsolescence and alternate sourcing.
- Background in scientific instrumentation, aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability electronics production.
- Experience providing DFM and DFT feedback to hardware engineering teams.

title: WHS Manager, WHS Manager
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced and results-driven Multi-Site Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) Manager to lead the expansion, standardization, and compliance of WHS programs across our growing Sub-Same Day (SSD) delivery operations in Mexico. This is a strategic leadership role at the forefront of our operational growth, ensuring every new and existing site meets the highest safety standards from day one.

In this role, you will be the primary WHS leader responsible for driving a culture of safety across multiple sites. You will develop and administer compliance frameworks built on both leading indicators (proactive safety activities, training completion, hazard identification) and lagging indicators (incident rates, severity metrics, lost-time injuries), using data to anticipate risks before they materialize and to measure the effectiveness of corrective actions.

You will work hand-in-hand with operational teams to implement safety policies, ensure adherence to Amazon global WHS standards, and guarantee full compliance with Mexican federal and local regulations — including STPS NOMs, IMSS requirements, and Proteccion Civil mandates. Your ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and embed safety into every operational process will be critical to our success.

Effective Communication with Senior Leadership.

Primary WHS voice to Managers — concise 6-pagers and narratives

Influence without authority, earn trust through results

title: Associate Account Executive , SMB
descriptionHtml:
This is not your typical entry-level sales role — it's a launchpad.

At Amazon, our peculiar culture and obsession with delighting customers extends to everything we do, including what we call our teams. While the industry knows this role as a SDR, BDR, Associate Account Executive, Amazon's customer-first DNA means we call our team members "Customer Acquisition Representatives" (CARs). It's more than a name, it reflects our belief that every interaction should start and end with the customer. As a CAR, you'll accelerate pipeline growth, navigate complex customer landscapes, shift gears between strategic thinking and high-impact execution, and put customers in the driver's seat of their cloud journey. Every CAR needs fuel, yours will be curiosity, coaching, and the full support of the world's leading cloud platform.

As a CAR, you will take the lead in unlocking growth potential for both new and existing AWS customers. We are one of the principal sources of new pipeline that fuels the AWS engine – engaging the unengaged accounts and contacts to drive pipeline that turns into revenue. Using cutting-edge AI tools and data-driven insights, you'll identify whitespace opportunities and develop innovative strategies to reach unengaged accounts at scale. You'll be part of shaping how technology is deployed across thousands of organizations, from enabling rapid, individually customized cancer treatments to helping Fortune 500 companies meet their carbon emissions goals. The AWS technology stack is the backbone of some of the most innovative solutions to the world's most pressing problems.

Your career path is clear. This role is designed as the entry point into AWS's North American sales organization. We don't need the perfect candidate, but we do want people who are curious, coachable, and willing to learn. We've developed hundreds of early-career professionals into full cycle sellers as Cloud Sales Representatives (CSRs), many within 18–24 months. You'll be paired with mentors and have access to structured development programs that accelerate your growth from day one.

According to Gartner, AWS is the leading cloud provider in both ability to execute and completeness of vision. With only 5% of all IT spend in the cloud, we are still in the early stages of what is possible, and with the explosion of generative AI, the opportunity has never been larger. You'll be at the forefront, equipped with the most advanced AI-powered sales technology in the industry. Consider this your pit crew advantage — the tools, training, and teammates that keep you performing at your best.

title: Support Engineer, Identity and Access Management
descriptionHtml:
Do you have a passion for protecting data and ensuring compliance at scale? We are looking for a detail-oriented Support Engineers to join our data protection team, where you will investigate access to Amazon's most sensitive and regulated data. You will independently review SQL queries, access logs, and large datasets to determine compliance with policies and standard operating procedures, making clear determinations that protect customer trust and data integrity.

In this role, you will combine technical investigation skills with stakeholder engagement, interpreting complex access patterns and coaching teams on compliant data handling. You will evaluate access requests against data-handling policies, document findings with clarity and precision, and escalate high-risk cases with sound judgment. This is an opportunity to apply your analytical expertise to meaningful work that safeguards data across one of the world's largest technology platforms.

Key job responsibilities
- Investigate access to sensitive data by reviewing SQL queries and access records to determine what data was accessed and whether that access is compliant with policies and standard operating procedures
- Interpret dashboards, logs, and large code and data sets to reach clear compliance determinations, applying analytical reasoning to identify patterns and assess risk
- Engage stakeholders and other Amazon employees to understand access behavior, remediate non-compliant practices, and share best practices that help them maintain compliance and keep data access safe
- Process access requests to protected data, evaluating internal use cases against data-sharing and data-handling policies to ensure appropriate access controls
- Document investigation findings clearly and concisely, articulating impact, the steps taken, and the current state of each case, and escalate complex or high-risk findings with sound judgment following information security guidelines

A day in the life
Much of your day is investigative work: reviewing SQL queries and access records to determine what data was accessed and whether that access is compliant with policy and standard operating procedures. Some investigations involve engaging stakeholders to understand access, remediate behavior, and coach them on compliance best practices. You will process requests for access to protected data, evaluating use cases against data-handling policy. Where needed, you will write queries to validate findings across datasets. As you build expertise, you will resolve cases independently and seek guidance from experienced engineers when cases are complex or findings are high-risk.

This role includes occasional on-call responsibilities.

Our Worldwide Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. Rapid and Rural Logistics (R2L) is an exciting organization within Amazon specializing in delighting our customers with speed in which we can make items appear on their doorsteps. title: Instructional Designer, EU Learning Design Team
descriptionHtml:
About Amazon Logistics
Amazon opened its virtual doors in 1995 and strives to be Earth's most customer-centric company, where customers can find and discover anything they might want to buy online. We aim to exceed our customers' expectations by ensuring that their orders—no matter how large or small—are delivered as quickly, accurately, and cost-effectively as possible.

About the Role
The EU Learning Design team is looking for an Instructional Designer to own the creation and management of learning content for our T3+ and LDEV (Leadership Development) population.
You are a hands-on, "sleeves rolled up" content creator who is fluent in authoring tools—particularly Articulate Rise and Storyline—and who actively leverages AI to design, accelerate, and scale learning content. You will spend time on the ground to understand the operational working environment and translate it into engaging, high-quality content that serves every type of learner, integrated with our Learning Management Systems (LMS).
This is a high-impact, fast-paced role in a dynamic manufacturing and logistics environment. The ability to travel across the EU and UK&IE region, as and when required, is essential.


Key job responsibilities
• Own the end-to-end design, development, and lifecycle management of learning content for the T3+ and LDEV population.
• Author engaging e-learning using Articulate Rise and Storyline across multiple modalities (e-learning, instructor-led, blended, microlearning).
• Use AI tools to accelerate content design and development, from drafting and storyboarding to media generation, localization, and iteration, while maintaining quality and instructional rigor.
• Build and manage content integrations with Learning Management Systems and author to standards such as SCORM/xAPI.
• Apply instructional design methodologies and adult learning principles to content for diverse learning styles.
• Immerse yourself in the operational environment to ensure content is accurate, relevant, and grounded in real working conditions.
• Partner with operations leaders, L&D teams, and subject matter experts to gather requirements and validate content.
• Define and measure learning effectiveness, iterating on content based on data and stakeholder feedback.
• Manage multiple projects simultaneously, meeting deadlines in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
Basic Qualifications
• Proven experience as an Instructional Designer, including a track record of successfully designing content in a fast-paced manufacturing, logistics, or operational environment.
• Demonstrable, hands-on proficiency with Articulate Rise and Storyline (portfolio or work samples expected).
• Experience using AI tools to design, create, and scale learning content.
• Hands-on experience developing content and managing integrations with Learning Management Systems.
• Ability and willingness to travel across the EU/UK&IE region as required.
• Familiarity with SCORM/xAPI standards and LMS administration.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience designing leadership development or management-level (T3+/LDEV) content.
• Experience with additional authoring/media tools (e.g., Adobe Captivate, Vyond, Camtasia).
• Experience applying AI responsibly at scale (prompt design, quality control, review workflows).
• Experience measuring learning impact and applying data to improve content.
• Experience working across multiple countries, cultures, and languages within the EU region.


A day in the life
- Intake requests from Learning Field Excellence, LDEV, Learning Change Managers and other OPS and/or L&D partners.
- Pull content from SMEs, read Standard Operational Procedures (SOPs).
- Design and build e-learning in Articulate Rise and Storyline, using AI to accelerate drafting, media, and localization.
- Publish to the LMS (SCORM/xAPI) and troubleshoot integration.
- Analyze learning data and iterate; align standards with peer designers.

About the team
You'll join EU E2E Learning Design, the team that owns the end-to-end learning content production lifecycle across Amazon's EU business lines. From instructional design to graphic and media production and Associate customer support, we serve every learner segment; Associates, Managers, central functions, Leadership Development (LDEV), and third-party audiences.

Our mission is to translate Learning Path needs into high-quality, innovative, and engaging learning products that meet Amazon's business standards and drive real business and learner outcomes. We bring together Learning Experience Designers, Graphic/Media Designers, and Central Services into one integrated team, working closely with subject matter experts to turn complex operational information into clear, interactive content that people actually remember and use.

This role sits within our AMZL T3+ and Leadership Development (LDEV) space, designing content that helps our leaders grow and run world-class operations. Culturally, we're hands-on, collaborative, and quality-obsessed — early adopters of modern authoring tools (Articulate Rise and Storyline) and AI to design better content, faster, while raising the bar for each other and sharing wins as a team.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Instructional Design, Adult Learning, Learning Design Principles, Learning Science, Educational Psychology or a related field
- Experience in stakeholder and communication management
- Experience analyzing data metrics

Preferred qualifications

- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Master's degree
