title: Software Development Engineer II, AFT Sortation, AFT Mansort
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wondered how Amazon delivers millions of customer orders with exceptional speed and reliability? Behind every fast and on-time delivery is a complex network of software, infrastructure, robotics, and operational processes engineered to work seamlessly at scale.

Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) builds the software and infrastructure that power Amazon's world-class fulfillment centers. Our systems integrate with warehouse automation, machines, and human associates to orchestrate critical fulfillment processes across a global network. These technologies enable the movement of millions of inventory units and support billions of transactions, ensuring that customers receive the products they want, when they expect them.

About the Mansort Team

The Mansort team owns the manual sortation layer of Amazon's fulfillment network. Our systems determine where packages should be routed after packing and before reaching the outbound dock, enabling accurate and efficient movement of shipments through fulfillment centers.

We build and operate software responsible for sort plan generation, chute and destination assignment, and scan-and-sort workflows used by warehouse associates. Our systems operate on the fulfillment center floor across hundreds of buildings worldwide, where reliability, performance, and correctness directly influence operational efficiency and customer delivery promises.

Mansort operates in a technically demanding environment characterized by high transaction volumes, stringent low-latency requirements, and the need for continuous availability despite connectivity disruptions or upstream dependency failures. Correctness is equally critical: every sortation decision must accurately direct a package to its intended destination to prevent operational errors and missed transportation cutoffs.

Manual sortation complements Amazon's automated sortation capabilities by providing the flexibility and scalability needed to handle peak demand, support new geographies and fulfillment center formats, and accommodate diverse operational requirements that cannot always be addressed through fixed automation.

As Amazon continues to expand its global fulfillment network and introduce new supply chain capabilities, delivery models, and customer experiences, the Mansort team has an opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems, modernize existing systems, and build scalable, resilient solutions that support the future of fulfillment operations.

Key job responsibilities
Design and develop scalable systems by owning the architecture, design, implementation, testing, and deployment of distributed software systems operating in live fulfillment center environments.

Build high-throughput, low-latency services that meet stringent performance, scalability, and availability requirements.

Ensure operational reliability and correctness through robust sortation workflows, data integrity, routing accuracy, fault tolerance, and graceful degradation.

Solve complex business and technical problems using pragmatic engineering decisions, innovative solutions, and modern technologies.

Drive operational excellence by improving observability, monitoring, troubleshooting, and recovery mechanisms to minimize disruptions.

Collaborate with product managers, operations teams, process engineers, and partner engineering teams to improve fulfillment efficiency and customer experience.

Influence technical direction by contributing to architecture, engineering standards, and technical strategy within the team and broader organization.

Maintain high engineering standards by writing clean, maintainable, well-tested code and ensuring software quality, performance, security, and reliability.

Mentor engineers through knowledge sharing, design discussions, code reviews, and technical guidance to strengthen team capabilities.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

descriptionHtml:

title: Program Manager, Predictions & Machine Learning , NASC Flow, Labor And Tech
descriptionHtml:
Role Overview
The Predictions & Machine Learning charter within the Flow, Labor & Tech (FLT) team of NA Sort Centers is looking for a Program Manager to launch and drive programs related to predictive modeling and machine learning for labor demand forecasting. Come be part of the team that enables the NASC middle mile network to process eight billion+ packages for our customers.
The Predictions charter owns two flagship products — ARES and AARP — that power demand forecasting and labor capacity predictions across the sort center network. As a Program Manager on this charter, you will have the opportunity to work closely with experienced Product Managers, Data Scientists, and ML Engineers to drive improvements in prediction accuracy, model adoption, and operational decision-making at scale.
Position Scope & Impact
As a member of the FLT Products team, you will partner with multiple stakeholders — both within NASC (Operations, PXT, Planning teams) and across associated Tech teams — to create new programs that improve the accuracy and reliability of labor demand predictions. You will collaborate with Data Scientists and ML Engineers to translate model outputs into actionable insights for operations leaders.
The main focus of this role is driving programs and efforts in the Predictions charter for the middle mile network. You will lead programs to drive Ops knowledge and adoption of prediction tools, provide reporting on model performance and accuracy improvements, and contribute to greenfield development of ML-powered prediction capabilities.


Key job responsibilities
1. Focus on improving accuracy and reliability of prediction models (ARES, AARP), enhance model performance monitoring, and eliminate forecasting errors in the labor planning process.
2. Drive greenfield development of ML-powered prediction programs and ensure all product feature requests are routed to the appropriate Product Manager.
3. Support the training and launch of new prediction tools and model features, including troubleshooting of model-related errors and data anomalies.
4. Initiate and drive programs to improve Ops knowledge and adoption of prediction products (ARES, AARP) across the NASC network.
5. Partner with Data Scientists, ML Engineers, and Ops users to research business pain points and develop use cases for improvements in prediction accuracy and model coverage.
6. Determine success metrics, build model performance dashboards, and audit prediction accuracy on a weekly basis for mature and emerging ML workstreams.
7. Develop documentation and present model performance insights, program roadmaps, and strategic recommendations to L8-level stakeholders on a regular basis.
8. Determine initiatives that will standardize, centralize, and automate prediction pipelines and model deployment processes across the network.
9. Deep dive and root-cause prediction misses using data, create metrics-driven, actionable, and sustainable solutions to improve forecast reliability.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

- 3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience

title: Power Electronics Reliability Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a Power Electronics Reliability Engineer to own the functional-safety case and the reliability/qualification program for the SST control, protection and power-conversion system.

As a Power Electronics Reliability Engineer you will: 1) define IEC 61508 safety functions and safe-state behavior (STO/SS1/SLS), 2) plan/run HALT/HASS and qualification per the V&V strategy, and 3) deliver a defined safety and reliability scope. You will drive hazard analysis, diagnostic/watchdog requirements, fault-state management, failure analysis and root-cause, and derive MTBF/MTTR and reliability metrics with the required diagnostic coverage. You will maintain safety requirements and traceability, review implementation evidence, coordinate critical-component supplier qualification and corrective actions, and resolve issues across disciplines.

About AIS
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.


Key job responsibilities
Safety architecture:
- Apply IEC 61508 principles to safety-related embedded and control functions.
- Define safety functions and safe-state behavior.
- Coordinate safety requirements with system, FPGA, controls and embedded software architectures.

Protection mechanisms:
- Define and review STO, SS1 and SLS functions as applicable to the architecture.
- Define watchdog and embedded diagnostic requirements.
- Develop and review fault-state management strategies.

Safety lifecycle & verification:
- Maintain safety requirements and traceability.
- Support safety analysis and verification planning.
- Review implementation evidence and safety-related test results.
- Coordinate safety issue resolution across engineering disciplines.

Qualification:
- Plan and execute HALT/HASS and other qualification activities identified in the V&V strategy.
- Define reliability stresses and qualification conditions with engineering teams.
- Track qualification status and evidence.

Failure analysis:
- Perform and coordinate failure analysis.
- Identify recurring failure modes and recommend corrective actions.
- Feed reliability findings back into design margins, safe-state behavior and component selection.

Reliability metrics:
- Track MTBF/MTTR and other reliability indicators.
- Identify reliability and safety risks in critical components and subsystems.
- Use test and field data to prioritize reliability and safety improvements.

Supplier follow-up:
- Coordinate critical-component supplier follow-up.
- Review supplier qualification and reliability evidence.
- Support corrective actions for component-related failures.

SST System Alignment:
- Align the role with the system safety framework without treating SIL2 as a system requirement. system specification references NFPA, UL and IEEE electrical-safety standards; IEC 61508/SIL targets should be established by the product safety strategy if applicable.
- Cover functional protection, fault-state behavior, safe restart inhibition, insulation-monitoring interactions, arc-flash considerations and diagnostic coverage.
- Translate system 15+ year design-life and environmental/structural expectations into reliability stresses and qualification plans.
- Include redundancy/catcher behavior, degradation warnings, fault recovery, thermal derating and critical MV/HV insulation components in both safety and reliability analysis.

A day in the life
In this role, you'll focus on establishing safety architectures and reliability programs for our Solid State Transformer control and protection systems. Your day might include defining safety functions according to IEC 61508 standards, coordinating with embedded software and FPGA teams to align safety requirements with system design, or planning qualification activities like HALT/HASS testing.

You'll analyze field data and test results to identify reliability trends, work with component suppliers to resolve critical issues, and document your findings to inform design improvements. You'll also participate in cross-functional problem-solving sessions where your expertise helps resolve complex safety and reliability challenges that span electrical, software, and systems engineering disciplines.

About the team


Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to celebrate our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and diversity conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We have a career path for you no matter what stage you’re in when you start here. We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related experience/ field.
- Reliability-engineering experience in power electronics or industrial systems.
- Experience with IEC 61508 and functional-safety development and/or embedded systems and diagnostics experience.
- Experience documenting design decisions, assumptions, trade-offs, risks and technical specifications.
- Experience using engineering analysis and measured evidence demonstrating strong data-driven problem solving.
- Experience demonstrating maintaining a strong focus on safety, reliability, serviceability and scalable deployment.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering.
- Experience in functional safety (IEC 61508/62061-class) and/or reliability & qualification engineering for electrical/power-electronics systems, including verification.
- Experience with HALT/HASS and failure analysis.
- Demonstrated understanding of safe-state behavior, watchdogs, fault-state management, MTBF/MTTR and reliability metrics.
- Experience working with FPGA, controls and embedded-software teams, and coordinating critical component suppliers.
- Demonstrated operating effectively in a greenfield environment where standards and reference designs may require interpretation and adaptation.

title: CFD/Thermal Simulation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a CFD/Thermal Simulation Engineer to develop thermal and CFD models to predict, optimize and validate the thermal performance of the 5–10 MW SST.

As a CFD/Thermal Simulation Engineer you will build 3D CFD (Icepak / Fluent / COMSOL / Simcenter) and thermal-resistance models predicting SST thermal performance on a defined project. You will handle conjugate heat transfer, mesh/fidelity trade-offs, hotspot prediction and junction-margin analysis under variable load and correlate to measurement and feed optimized designs to thermal/mechanical and PE teams.



Key job responsibilities
CFD modeling:
- Build 3D thermal simulations using Icepak, ANSYS Fluent, COMSOL, Simcenter or equivalent tools.
- Model heat transfer through power electronics, cooling interfaces and system assemblies.
- Evaluate thermal distribution, hotspots and cooling-system performance.
Thermal modeling:
- Develop thermal-resistance models and junction-to-coolant analyses.
- Support semiconductor and component thermal-margin definition.
- Analyze thermal behavior under variable load profiles.
Correlation & optimization:
- Correlate simulation results with experimental measurements.
- Use test results to refine models and identify design improvements.
- Support thermal design optimization with Mechanical and Power Electronics teams.
SST System Alignment:
- Model system environmental conditions and thermal derating, including -30°C to 40°C ambient and above-40°C derating requirements.
- Correlate thermal models with efficiency, load-profile and qualification data across the SST operating envelope.


A day in the life
As a CFD/Thermal Simulation Engineer, you'll focus on building sophisticated 3D thermal simulations that predict how heat flows through power electronics and cooling systems. Your day might include developing conjugate heat transfer models using tools like Icepak, ANSYS Fluent, COMSOL, or Simcenter, then correlating your simulation results with real laboratory measurements to refine designs. You'll collaborate with mechanical and power electronics teams to identify hotspots, analyze thermal behavior under different operating conditions, and translate your findings into actionable design improvements. You'll also work across variable environmental conditions—from extreme cold to high ambient temperatures—ensuring systems perform reliably throughout their operating envelope.

You'll be part of a group that values continuous learning, embraces diverse perspectives, and supports your growth as you solve problems that matter at scale.

We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

- Demonstrated understanding of power-electronics thermal behavior.
- Experience and ability to correlate models with laboratory measurements.
- Experience documenting design decisions, assumptions, trade-offs, risks and technical specifications.
- Experience using engineering analysis and measured evidence to drive decisions.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering.
- 2+ years experience in CFD/thermal simulation for electronics cooling with measured correlation.
- Experience with Icepak, ANSYS Fluent, COMSOL or Simcenter.
- Demonstrated working effectively with adjacent engineering disciplines and contribute to full A-to-Z product ownership.

title: Senior Software Dev Engineer, Route 53 Health Checks and Console Core
descriptionHtml:
Build the service that checks the health of millions of endpoints around the world every few seconds, and the consoles customers rely on to run DNS and route traffic at global scale. As a Senior SDE on the Amazon Route 53 Health Checks and Console Core team, you will own the technical direction for the team and drive the plan with leadership, lead how we use AI to design, build, test, and operate software, and grow the engineers around you. You will own the distributed health checking infrastructure and the public API in front of it, build the AI tooling every Route 53 service team depends on, and launch new AI services for DNS and Route 53. You will help define what our customers use next.

We are based in Vancouver, BC. We own Route 53 Health Checks, a highly available endpoint monitoring service that helps Route 53 DNS, Amazon Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon RDS, Amazon S3, and many other AWS services maintain high availability for their customers. We also own the core tooling, standards, and shared infrastructure that every Route 53 console is built on. This is a full stack role. You will design and operate the services and APIs behind Route 53 Health Checks, and you will take our console tooling from something our team uses to something every Route 53 service team builds on, while we hold the quality bar on what ships. Your work will reach across more than 10 service teams and the product managers, designers, and engineers you partner with throughout AWS networking.

AI is central to how we work and what we build. As a senior engineer on the team, you will own how we work with it. You will define the AI development process the team runs on across coding, testing, and operations, decide which tools and practices we adopt, measure whether they make us faster and safer, and roll what works out to the service teams that build on our platform. You will own the results of the team, not only your own code. You will drive our yearly plan, turn goals into projects with milestones and estimates, sequence the work across the team, and track it to delivery. When a plan slips or a risk shows up, you raise it early and change the plan. You will lead projects that span several engineers, drive the designs behind them, and mentor engineers through design reviews and code reviews.


Key job responsibilities
- Own the technical direction and the roadmap for the team, and lead projects that span several engineers from requirements to launch.
- Drive the yearly plan for the team with leadership, break goals into projects with milestones and estimates, and recommend what the team builds first
- Track delivery across the team, raise risks early, and adjust the plan when priorities or dependencies change.
- Define and run the AI development process for the team across coding, testing, and operations, and roll it out to service teams across Route 53.
- Mentor and grow the engineers on the team, and raise the bar through design reviews, code reviews, and operational reviews.
- Design, build, and operate the distributed health checking infrastructure and public API behind Route 53 Health Checks.
- Build and vend the AI tooling that service teams across Route 53 use to design and build their own console changes, and hold the quality bar on what they ship.
- Own and build new AI services and capabilities for DNS and Route 53, from idea to launch.
- Operate what you build. Take part in on call, own metrics and alarms, and drive root cause analysis on production issues.
- Work with product managers, designers, and engineers across more than 10 service teams in AWS networking.
- Turn requirements that are ambiguous and change quickly into products customers rely on.
Our health checking stack is primarily Java and Linux, with lots of interaction with public AWS services and Amazon internal tools. Our console stack is TypeScript and React. We do not expect you to know all of it, but we do expect you to be excited to learn it.

A day in the life
Our customers are the developers and businesses who use Route 53 to manage DNS and route traffic for their applications around the world, and our job is to make that easy, reliable, and fast. No two days look the same. You might start the morning reviewing a design with an engineer you mentor, then work with the team on a new AI practice to cut the time from idea to production. After lunch you might review a change a service team submitted and hold the bar on the console patterns and the design guidelines, then spend the rest of the afternoon on the health checking infrastructure itself, on the checkers that monitor millions of endpoints or the public API in front of them. Some days you go deep on a distributed system, other days you are building tooling or trying out a new AI tool and deciding whether the team should adopt it. You drive the plan for what the team builds next with leadership, track how it is going, and partner with service teams across AWS networking to ship features that reach customers everywhere. When a hackathon idea grabs you, there is room to chase it.


About the team
We are a tight knit team that cares about our customers and about running a highly available platform on the Internet. We like to experiment and to learn out loud, whether that is a hackathon, a demo of something you just built, or a session digging into a new AI tool together. We are good at making sense of ambiguity and shipping products people rely on, and we welcome bold ideas and give you the ownership to take them all the way. And when we are not building, we make time to have fun together with regular team outings.

If you want to lead hard problems at scale, help shape the plan for a team that builds with AI, and help decide where an AWS service goes next, we would like to hear from you.

- 7+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- 7+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 7+ years of highly scalable systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

title: Site HR Partner Manager, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wanted to be part of a team building industry-changing technology? At Leo, we are building a low Earth orbit satellite network that will deliver broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities. Come join one of Amazon's most ambitious bets, with customers like Delta Airlines, JetBlue, AT&T, and others already committed ahead of commercial launch.
We are seeking an HRP Manager to lead the Site HR Partners who serve Leo's Production Operations (ProdOps) organization. You will own the standards the team operates against and the forward-looking model for how site HRP partnership evolves as the business grows. Every satellite is a one-way-door decision, and the pace demands manager excellence as a precondition to mission success.
This is not a standard corporate HR role. ProdOps is 24/7 aerospace manufacturing, where technicians build every satellite the business pushes to Launch Services, and where the managers your team serves are navigating the intersection of Amazon's people culture with the operational discipline of building satellites. Many are external hires with deep technical expertise who are still building fluency in how Amazon develops people, or Amazon veterans encountering manufacturing realities for the first time. Site HRPs deliver capabilities not found in traditional corporate HRP roles: proactive sentiment reading through weekly floor walks and Gembas, time-sensitive labor relations work in a high ER/LR environment, round-the-clock shift coverage, and direct coaching on how to lead where the stakes are measured in millions of dollars per week.
In this role, you will directly manage a team of Site HRPs across the production sites and shifts, and you will own their development end to end: coaching their strategic judgment, functional skill, and advisory craft so they operate as independent partners rather than conduits. You will think ahead of the business, anticipating what the workforce and the Site HRP model need to look like at scale and building toward that before the demand arrives. As the network grows to establish dedicated presence across sites, extends into evening and overnight coverage, and absorbs net-new facility stand-ups, your central charge is to make sure the team on the floor is developed, consistent, operating to one standard, and ready for what comes next.
This role reports to the Sr. HRP Manager (Leo), who owns the integrated Corp, Site, and Launch Services HRP delivery model and the multi-year ProdOps HRP strategy. You own the site HRP strategy, how the team is developed, and how the model scales within that framework. The role requires regular travel to production sites to work alongside your team, understand evolving business challenges, and maintain strong relationships with operational leadership.


Key job responsibilities
• Lead and Develop the Site HRP Team. Directly manage a team of Site HRPs supporting the hourly manufacturing workforce across production sites and shifts. Demonstrate a clear understanding of the performance and leadership bar and apply it to hiring and talent decisions. Provide regular coaching and feedback that grows each HRP’s strategic judgment, functional skill, and leadership capability, and build a team that delivers with increasing independence as the network scales.
• Own Site HRP Ways of Working and the Standard of Excellence. Define and run the frameworks, mechanisms, and quality standards the Site HRP team operates against, including how floor walks, Gembas, structured listening, and case work are delivered consistently across every site and shift. Build the inspection mechanisms that ensure advisory quality, sound judgment, and timely closure across the team’s portfolio.
• Deliver Consistent, High-Quality Manager Guidance Across Sites and Shifts. Own the Site HRP team’s metrics and the manager customer experience. Review the guidance and case work the team handles to ensure quality, sound judgment, and timely closure, and coach the team to synthesize inputs into action and communicate risk proactively. The scope of guidance spans performance management, employee relations, talent decisions, compensation guidance, policy consultation, and crisis support.
• Build Manager Capability Through Scalable Mechanisms. Design and run scalable mechanisms that build manager capability over time (manager enablement, structured coaching such as Seek to Understand, and proactive insight tools) so ProdOps managers lead effective teams with growing confidence and self-sufficiency, strengthening the manager population rather than resolving one case at a time.
• Partner on Employee Relations Strategy and Prevention. Partner with GCER and Legal and provide guidance and oversight to the team on ER cases, ensuring sound judgment, timely closure, and adherence to a high bar on ER metrics. Set the standard for how the team navigates complex workplace investigations and uses embedded floor presence to resolve concerns before they escalate into formal cases.
• Scale the Site HRP Model Without Ground-Up Rebuilds. As the Site network grows (dedicated presence across sites, extended evening and overnight coverage, and net-new facility stand-ups), build the onboarding, coverage, and ways-of-working standards that absorb growth without rebuilding from scratch, ensuring coverage and development are operational ahead of each new site’s first technicians.
• Measure, Inspect, and Advance AI-First Delivery. Translate operational data into systemic insight through dashboards and trend analysis that surface employee-experience signal before it becomes escalation, and champion AI-first ways of working (for example Amazon Quick and self-service through Aza) that shift team capacity from reactive case handling toward proactive, capability-building advisory work.

- Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Human Resources Management, Labor Relations, Business/Management, Psychology, or a related field
- 7+ years of relevant Human Resources Generalist experience
- 2+ years of management experience implementing processes and delivering core HR solutions in large-scale and complex environments
- Experience coaching and developing HR professionals and building team capability

- Experience supporting manufacturing, aerospace, or hardware engineering organizations with both exempt and non-exempt populations

title: Signal Integrity Engineer, Amazon Devices
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Lab126 is an inventive research and development company that designs and engineers high-profile devices like the Kindle family of products. Lab126 began in 2004 as a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc. Since then, we have worked to produce best-selling e-readers and tablets, as well as new inventions like Echo line of products, Fire TV and Fire phone. What will you help us create?

Key job responsibilities
As a Signal Integrity Engineer, you will be part of Validation team that is exploring new hardware designs to improve our devices. In this role, you will be responsible for Signal Integrity aspects, compliance, and interoperability of package substrate, PCB, Cable solutions and system-level SI for interfaces like PCIe, DDR, Clocks etc. You will also be responsible for contributing to package and platform design guideline development.

You will work closely with multi-disciplinary groups including Board Design, System Architects, IP developers, and Design Engineering, to verify and deliver complex, high volume SoCs that enable development of world-class hardware devices. In this role, you will be:
• Responsible for defining the design guidelines for internal and external design teams and delivering reference simulation docs for customers
• Performing modeling of package substrate/PCB channels elements in 3D/2D EM simulation tools.
• Working with silicon designers, platform designers, package designers, electrical validation teams, etc. to support interconnect and interface performance requirements.
• Reviewing and evaluating package and board design and providing review feedback.
• Responsible for providing power delivery solutions across platform, package and SOC level
• Definition of worst-case currents and voltage drop scenarios, MIM/decoupling allocation, grid choices and analysis, droop control, SOC ESD compliance, On-die droop detectors, usage of on-die delivery solutions like VR, LDO, and Power gates.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
- 4+ years of hardware design and validation of components, subsystems and systems experience
- High speed serial interface analog building blocks, protocol, specifications and test methods
- Familiarity with Simulation tools (ADS, HFSS, PowerSI, PowerDC, Hyperlynx) to execute SI-PI simulations is required.
- Experience with performing measurement, and correlating measurements to simulations.
- Experience with modeling and simulation of high-speed interface interconnects/channel.
- Excellent analytical and problem solving skills

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Electrical or Communications Engineering or a related field
- Understanding of Power & signal integrity concepts such as differential impedance, jitter, insertion loss, return loss, termination, etc.
- Scripting experience in any programming language (C++, Python, PERL, MATLAB) to develop automation scripts is a plus.
- Experience in Analog IP Characterization (SerDes, PLL, DDR) is desirable.
- Good understanding of High-Speed Analog/Digital Circuits, VLSI, semiconductor physics

descriptionHtml:

Specialist Solutions Architects work with AWS' partners and customers to accelerate their cloud transformation. They engage in a wide range of activities around their domain of expertise, providing technical advice to customers, helping the internal and external communities, presenting AWS publicly on their domain, and providing a preferred path between AWS service teams and customers.

This is an opportunity to join Amazon's technical teams, working with our engineers on the new services that power the cloud ecosystem, while developing your skills and furthering your career within what we believe to be one of the most innovative and progressive technology companies. This role will specifically focus on the Migration and Modernization aspects of AWS Services and on helping our customers and partners build innovative and secure Solutions and Businesses.

As a Migration and Modernization Specialist Solutions Architect (SA), you will help customers select the technologies that will support their business requirements. Part of the Specialist Solutions Architecture team, you will work closely with the other Specialist SAs on Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, and Modern Applications Development, as well as the Business Development teams, to enable large-scale customer use cases and drive the adoption of AWS for their platforms. You will interact with other SAs, providing guidance on their customer engagements by developing white papers, blogs, reference implementations, and presentations to enable customers and 3rd party to fully leverage the AWS platform. title: Senior Product Manager, Technical, Identity
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to define the future of how hundreds of millions of Amazon customers prove who they are? AI-powered attacks are making passwords and legacy multi-factor authentication increasingly vulnerable, and our Identity team is responding by building the next generation of authentication — passkeys, digital IDs, phishing-resistant phone-number verification, and more. As a Senior Product Manager, Technical on this team, you will own the end-to-end product lifecycle for these new authentication experiences, from problem discovery through launch and optimization, across surfaces including desktop, mobile, TV, and smart-home devices.

You will combine deep customer empathy with rigorous metrics analysis to understand how customers sign in, where friction exists, and what solutions will earn their trust. You will partner with engineering, design, legal, and cross-functional stakeholders to ship experiences that protect customers while keeping interactions simple and intuitive. If you are energized by solving complex security challenges at massive scale and want your work to be felt every time a customer interacts with Amazon, we would love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and evolve the authentication product strategy — assess customer needs, market trends, and emerging threats to set a clear vision for passwordless and phishing-resistant experiences across your area of ownership.
- Own the product roadmap from concept to launch, prioritizing initiatives based on customer impact and business value while managing cross-functional dependencies with engineering, design, and legal teams.
- Write detailed product requirements, user stories, and success criteria; partner with designers on prototypes and with engineers on architecture reviews to ensure solutions are scalable, secure, and intuitive.
- Analyze adoption metrics, customer behavior data, and performance indicators to identify optimization opportunities, root-cause issues, and inform roadmap investments.
- Collaborate with senior leaders, partner teams, and stakeholders across the company to build alignment on new authentication initiatives and influence organization-wide priorities.

A day in the life
Your morning might start by reviewing authentication success-rate dashboards and digging into an anomaly you spotted in passkey enrollment metrics. After a design review for a new digital ID verification flow, you join your engineering team's sprint planning to refine acceptance criteria and discuss technical trade-offs. descriptionHtml:

This role is a key member of the Energy Accounting team, supporting technical evaluations for derivative accounting. Operating in an environment where strategy may not be fully defined, the individual will use expertise and judgment to select the right stakeholders, determine goals, and drive resolution of complex accounting questions. The individual will:

- Draft technical GAAP accounting position papers addressing complex topics, including derivatives/financial instruments (ASC 815), fair value measurement (ASC 820), leasing (ASC 842), consolidation (ASC 810), and commitments (ASC 440), consulting with accounting policy as appropriate
- Research and document complex accounting concepts in clear, concise, and unambiguous language that critically supports proposed conclusions

- Support the period-end close process by ensuring accurate and timely completion of all derivative-related accounting entries, reconciliations, and analytical reviews

- Identify, validate, and lead opportunities for standardization of processes across teams
- Drive productivity by simplifying processes, engaging emerging technology, and/or implementing innovative solutions

- Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages

Preferred qualifications

title: Pre-Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Preconstruction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's owner's representative during the preconstruction phase — responsible for independently managing difficult, cross-functional industrial building projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution across your assigned region. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You are responsible as the project manager to lead planning, design, and preconstruction projects — including new built-to-suit industrial buildings, tenant improvements, extensions of existing facilities, and renovation projects — supporting Amazon's logistics network infrastructure.

You work independently within your assigned region, using your knowledge of construction and project management concepts to decide which actions to take to complete projects, and seeking guidance as needed on strategic components. You are tactical with some strategic components, utilizing well-defined processes and best practices to facilitate delivery of high-quality results. You make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources to keep projects on track.

Key competencies of this position include ensuring that contracted resources deliver work product in support of project durations, permitting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and quality documentation; managing project teams (developers, design engineers, professional consultants); influencing internal teams (Design Engineering, Amazon Robotics); contract management governance; conceptual estimating and budget oversight; and managing multiple large industrial projects in various locations simultaneously. Translating technical documents and information into clear, concise narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers is essential.

This opportunity combines construction engineering, planning, project management, real estate development, design validation, site visits, understanding of local building and fire code issues, utilities, sustainability, multi-disciplinary design management, and contract management. The Preconstruction Manager is responsible for the planning and design of scope, budget, and schedule prior to handing off to the Construction Manager — focusing on taking ownership to resolve upstream issues and supporting the construction team throughout the process.

This role requires 60% regional travel on a yearly basis. When not traveling, you must have availability to work from a corporate office. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of one of the corporate office locations listed. Relocation assistance may be provided.


Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Supervise the implementation and management of Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams during the planning and preconstruction phases of a project
- Interface and coordinate with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Review noise, traffic, and environmental studies; understand zoning, planning, fire code, and building code requirements for assigned projects

Preconstruction & Project Management
- Independently manage difficult, cross-functional industrial preconstruction projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution
- Lead site selection and validation, scope development, and design management — coordinating with design teams to develop site plans and composite floor plans in compliance with Amazon's design standards and operational requirements
- Manage multiple concurrent large industrial projects across various locations simultaneously
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately
- Identify and resolve upstream issues proactively to support a clean handoff to the Construction Manager; remain a key support resource for the construction team throughout the project lifecycle
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability
- Minimize disruptions and proactively mitigate risks; plan ahead to prevent problems before they happen

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Develop and manage project budgets and costs; own comprehensive schedule management and cashflow forecasting across assigned preconstruction projects
- Perform conceptual estimating and pricing reviews for scope inclusions and exclusions; negotiate the cost of work with developers, general contractors, and design consultants
- Contribute to the selection of external vendor partners and manage vendor procurement; oversee professional service providers to ensure their skills and competencies meet project requirements
- Review and analyze design and construction contracts, related exhibits, and lease agreements; provide detailed analysis of technical matters and site-specific deal structures and terms
- Partner with the Transaction team and developers to optimize schedule and strategy for entitlements and long-lead procurement
- Identify and solve factors that may impede a successful permitted project handover to Amazon stakeholders; make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Drive results through communicating, weighing risks, making decisions, leading, and influencing; competently represent project and technical information to diverse audiences
- Maintain good working relationships with stakeholders and vendors; lead constructive dialogue to resolve and prevent project issues
- Act as the primary escalation point for project team members; own and track issues to ensure they are addressed, documented, and resolved

Communication & Reporting
- Prepare and present project status and risk reports; provide clear, concise summaries for projects under your ownership to leadership and management teams
- Translate technical documents and information into end-to-end narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, checking progress, and driving high-level alignment and consensus
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners; trusted to present decisions to leaders up to 2-3 tiers above level
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

Process Improvement & Innovation
- Optimize preconstruction processes and implement improvements in procedures and playbooks to improve project efficiency and delivery
- Look for opportunities to improve operational excellence and influence the team to determine where to iterate and make improvements
- Seek sustainable, environmentally responsible solutions throughout the preconstruction process in alignment with Amazon's building practices
- Adapt to constant change and innovation; find adaptable solutions for an evolving business

A day in the life
Each day, you represent GES NA Design & Construction as Amazon's owner during the preconstruction phase — navigating uncertainty, proactively unblocking project barriers, and influencing the best project decisions. You are tactical with some strategic components, working independently and interacting with leadership to resolve issues. Your day may include:
- Coordinating with architects, engineers, and design consultants on design document development, scope changes, and project status
- Reviewing site plans, composite floor plans, and design documents for compliance with Amazon's standards and operational requirements
- Negotiating contract terms with developers, contractors, and consultants while driving adherence to schedules and budgets
- Coordinating with AHJ on permitting status, zoning, fire code, and building code requirements
- Preparing and presenting project status and risk reports for leadership
- Partnering with Real Estate and Transaction teams on entitlement strategy and long-lead procurement
- Providing estimating support, interpreting drawings, contributing to budgets, and reviewing lease exhibits
- Updating Amazon's project management systems with current budget, schedule, and status information
- Supporting the Construction Manager on active construction projects with preconstruction expertise

About the team
At Amazon, the GES North America Design & Construction team is a diverse group of engineers, construction managers, and preconstruction professionals who deliver the physical infrastructure behind Amazon's logistics network. We are employee owners who take pride in delivering high-quality, innovative facilities — on time and on budget — for our internal customers and the communities we serve. We are committed to being Earth's best employer and to building a more sustainable future through every project we deliver.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's Project Management Representative, or in a related commercial development or construction discipline
- 5+ years of project management experience from design phase through implementation and operation, including negotiating construction, procurement, and labor contracts
- Experience within packaging, processing, or logistical facilities with complex equipment, or comparable experience
- Position includes travel up to 60% (Nationwide). Travel involves air travel to regional airports and driving to site locations. A valid driver's license is required due to project assignments in areas with limited public transportation and rideshare options.

Preferred qualifications

- Advanced degree or certification in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or Business Administration
- Experience operating across at least two disciplines within the construction industry (e.g., General Contracting, Owner's Representation, Commercial Development, Engineering & Design, or Owner's Project Management)
- Demonstrated capability in planning, design review, implementation, and project management/control of new structures and enhancement of existing facilities
- Experience managing multi-disciplinary design incorporating industrial automation, robotics, or similar
- Strong influencing and negotiating skills
- Demonstrated success communicating project requirements to diverse audiences (e.g., senior management, peers, fire marshals, utility providers, public officials, vendors)
- Knowledge of Building Information Modeling (BIM)
- CMIT/CMAA or PMP certification or equivalent

title: Senior Principal Engineer , AWS Billing
descriptionHtml:
How cloud customers experience billing — from the pricing they see, to the costs they manage, to the bills they pay — is foundational to how they trust and grow with AWS. Today, that experience is ready for a transformation: one that brings the commercial simplicity of amazon.com to the cloud, in near real-time, across every customer segment. Are you ready to define the technical strategy that makes that possible?



About the Team

AWS Billing is responsible for processing all AWS revenue — computing millions of bills daily and reliably handling billions of usage records per second across every AWS service, customer, and partner worldwide. Our systems ensure that financial data is fully auditable, accurate, and timely, while simultaneously adapting to evolving pricing models, contract structures, and regulatory environments.

We are at an inflection point. Small customers need pricing simplicity, cost predictability, and real-time visibility into their usage — so they can use AWS without fear of surprise costs. Large enterprise and government customers need commercial flexibility, configurable pricing, and democratized cost management. New opportunities are emerging to externalize our billing and pricing capabilities as a platform, and to support new pricing models that give AWS the commercial agility required to stay competitive. Increasingly, the systems we build will also need to serve autonomous agents interacting with billing, pricing, and cost data in fundamentally different ways than humans do today. These challenges are not met well by any cloud provider today, so there is a lot to invent.

Key job responsibilities

Define and own the multi-year technical strategy for billing architecture, partnering with engineering leaders and scientists across the organization to guide the next generation of billing systems — more composable, more adaptable, and built to evolve at the velocity the business requires.
Drive architectural decisions that span multiple organizations across AWS service teams, Marketplace, Sales, and Finance, ensuring alignment on how billing systems transform from batch-oriented financial processing into a real-time platform.
Provide technical guidance across billing and commerce teams, increasing productivity and effectiveness through deep knowledge of distributed systems, real-time processing, enterprise architecture, and generative AI technology.
Ensure the quality of architecture and design across billing systems by decomposing complex problems into straightforward, scalable solutions, with a focus on performance optimization and engineering practices that enable systems to scale seamlessly.
Mentor engineers and the broader community on advanced distributed systems challenges, helping develop technical talent across billing engineering teams while maintaining a pragmatic focus on business outcomes.


A day in the life
You will balance understanding the nuances of how customers — from startups to the world's largest enterprises — interact with AWS billing and cost management, while shaping the architectural vision that makes those experiences seamless. On any given day, you may lead a design review for a next-generation pricing engine, align with partner teams on integration patterns for a new AWS service launch, or work hands-on with engineers to prototype a real-time billing pipeline. You will navigate competing stakeholder priorities while maintaining a high bar for accuracy, performance, operational resilience, and system efficiency. You will also play a key role in shaping how the engineering organization leverages AI to accelerate development, testing, and delivery across the billing platform.

Basic qualifications


Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
15+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems in a multi-tiered, service-oriented environment
Experience defining and driving multi-year technical strategy across multiple engineering teams

Preferred qualifications


Master's degree or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
Experience with high-volume data processing systems, real-time computation, or financial/billing systems at scale
Experience modeling complex pricing, contractual, or regulatory business rules in software
Familiarity with generative AI technologies and their application to software development workflows

title: Applied Scientist, Amazon Robotics
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Robotics is seeking an exceptional Applied Scientist to join our Foundation Models and Agentic AI team. This role presents an opportunity to shape the future of robotics through innovative applications of large vision-language-action (VLA) models, reasoning and task planning models, and reinforcement learning.

At Amazon Robotics, we leverage advanced robotics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to solve complex operational challenges at unprecedented scale. Our fleet of robots operates across hundreds of facilities worldwide, working in sophisticated coordination to fulfill our mission of customer excellence.

We are pioneering the development of robotics foundation models that:

- Enable unprecedented generalization across diverse tasks
- Integrate multi-modal learning capabilities (visual, depth, force, tactile, linguistic)
- Accelerate policy skill acquisition through imitation learning and reinforcement learning
- Enhance robotic perception and environmental understanding
- Streamline development processes through reusable capabilities

The ideal candidate will contribute to research that bridges the gap between theoretical advancement and practical implementation in robotics. You will be part of a team that's revolutionizing how robots learn, adapt, and interact with their environment.

Join us in building the next generation of intelligent robotics systems that will transform the future of automation and human-robot collaboration.

Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Scientist in the Applied AI and Robotics Foundations Model team, you will:
- Model Development and Training: Designing and implementing the model architectures, training and fine tuning the foundation models using various datasets, and optimize the model performance through iterative experiments
- Data Management: Process and prepare training data, including data governance, provenance tracking, data quality checks and creating reusable data pipelines.
- Experimentation and Validation: Design and execute experiments to test model capabilities on the simulator and on the embodiment, validate performance across different scenarios, create a baseline and iteratively improve model performance.
- Code Development: Write clean, maintainable, well commented and documented code, contribute to training infrastructure, create tools for model evaluation and testing, and implement necessary APIs
- Research: Stay current with latest developments in foundation models and robotics, assist in literature reviews and research documentation, prepare technical reports and presentations, and contribute to research discussions and brainstorming sessions.
- Collaboration: Work closely with senior scientists, engineers, and leaders across multiple teams, participate in knowledge sharing, support integration efforts with robotics hardware teams, and help document best practices and methodologies.

title: Lead ASIC Modem Design Engineer, Satellite Communication
descriptionHtml:

Amazon Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.

Come work at Amazon!

The Role:
Be part of Leo's sub-team responsible for defining and implementing the digital chip SOCs for communications via Low Earth Orbit satellites and Amazon gateways. This is a unique opportunity to define a state-of-the-art wireless solution with few legacy constraints. The team works with customer requirements and wireless system teams to define modems, high-speed interfaces, embedded processors, and DSP solutions in latest CMOS generation technologies.

•Implement wireless system architecture in silicon from system specification to microarchitecture to RTL implementation to optimizing timing / power to chip level validation.
•Develop solutions optimizing customer experience (throughput, latency, and availability) while meeting power and cost constraints.
•Drive high quality designs for first-time right silicon solutions, and meeting the power objectives
•Create standalone verification test bench to verify the correctness of your block.
•Work with the verification team and participate in System level verification using test benches constructed using UVM, System C and DPI-C.
•Ensure that the block meets DFT, timing and power targets by working closely with the implementation team.
•Learn about requirements and solutions for systems operating in space
•Drive trade-off analysis to benefit customer experience and optimization of resources (costs, power, spectrum).
•Define specifications and architecture/micro-architecture for modem PHY subsystem blocks, including signal processing data paths.

• Involve in control plane logic design and interfaces to bus fabrics.
• Explore and propose innovative ideas and work towards optimization of the modem.
• Work closely with PHY-MAC boundary teams, software teams, and system integration teams to resolve complex HW-SW interaction issues.
• Support emulation platforms for early software development and system-level validation of modem IP.
• Mentor and assign work to junior team members.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical/Communications Engineering, or experience working in electrical engineering field
- 7+ years of experience in digital logic design, preferably in DSP or communication systems.

Preferred qualifications

- Master's or Ph.D degree in Electrical / Communications Engineering.
- 7+ years of experience in digital design, preferably in communication systems.
- Familiarity with UVM and Matlab.
- Knowledge of wireless communication standards (e.g., 5G NR, LTE, DVB-S2/S2X, or satellite communication protocols).
- Experience with ASIC design tools such as Cadence, Synopsys, or Mentor Graphics for synthesis, timing analysis, and physical design flows.

The Leo Customer Terminal Application and Networking Team builds the on-device software that runs on the customer's antenna and turns it into a fast, reliable, self-diagnosing internet gateway. As a Software Development Engineer II on this team, you will design and build software that operates on customer terminals deployed in the field at large scale — where there is no physical access and connectivity can be intermittent. title: Controls Coordinator, Asia-Pacific Controls Deployment & Service (APAC CDS)
descriptionHtml:
Are you someone who looks at a process and immediately sees what could be automated, documented better, or removed entirely? The Program Management and Coordination team within AWS Infrastructure Services is growing to support an expanding portfolio of data centre sites across Asia-Pacific, and we are looking for a Controls Coordinator to own the transactional backbone of controls delivery across APAC. You will manage every work order, change order, purchase request, purchase order, and capital appropriation request end to end against published SLAs, partnering with Controls Engineers, Finance, Legal, and Procurement to turn engineering decisions into committed spend.

The timing matters. The team is part-way through automating its own transactional work, so you will help design that tooling rather than inherit it finished. Vendor management is also becoming a defined programme rather than something each coordinator handles independently, giving you a clear area to own from the start. No data centre experience is needed. What matters is what you do with a process once you hold it: writing the run book a new joiner can follow without asking, building the report that answers the question before it gets asked, and automating the parts that should never have been manual.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage every work order, change order, purchase request, purchase order, and capital appropriation request end to end, tracking each against its published SLA and escalating exceptions early with a recommendation attached.
- Coordinate with Controls Engineers, Finance, Legal, and Procurement across APAC to land commitments that carry real money, including support for annual and mid-year operating plans.
- Design and maintain run books and process documentation so that workflows survive your absence and can be followed by any team member without additional guidance.
- Build reporting and automation that removes routine processing from people, using AI tools where they add value, and measure the before-and-after impact of every improvement you deliver.
- Own the vendor management programme for your region, defining consistent processes and partnering with global counterparts across a follow-the-sun operating model.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with your queue: the requests are yours from day one, and so are the blockers behind them. You might spend the first hour clearing purchase orders through their approval chain, then shift to refining an automation that shaves a manual step off the change-order workflow. After a standup with your Controls Engineering partners, you review an open vendor issue with Procurement and draft the escalation note. Later you pull together the data for a business review that senior leadership will read directly. Between tasks you are testing a new AI-driven dashboard the team is building in-house. By the end of the day you have moved work forward, removed a friction point, and documented what you changed so the next person does not have to ask.

About the team
The Program Management and Coordination team is the governance group within AWS Infrastructure Services that owns the planning cycles, goals, business reviews, and mechanisms the APAC region runs on. This is where process gets designed rather than requested. The team is eight people today, spread across Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney, and Melbourne, and everyone sits within the same Tech Ops Engineering job family — meaning the step from coordinator to programme manager is a genuine progression on a single ladder.

Our closest partners are the Controls Engineers running deployments, projects, service, and colocation across APAC, along with Finance, Legal, and Procurement on every commitment that carries money. We also collaborate with our counterparts in the Americas and EMEA through a global follow-the-sun model, so a process you improve once is improved everywhere we operate.

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our department, Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD), sponsors leadership programs that support the growth and development of builders across the organization. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events build stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation draws on the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Basic qualifications

- Experience producing written documentation, processes or reports that other people rely on without needing you to explain them
- Experience using generative AI tools in daily work, getting useful results from them on real tasks rather than experimenting
- Experience owning a queue or pipeline of transactional work against a deadline or a service level

Preferred qualifications

- Experience improving or standardising a process, with a measured before and after
- Experience working with data: extracting it, reconciling it and reporting on it, in spreadsheets, SQL or a business intelligence tool
- Experience building automation, whether with AI agents, workflow tools, low code platforms or scripts
- Experience in program or project management, including cross-functional delivery
- Experience reading and querying commercial contracts, purchase orders or invoices

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Global Procurement Technology
descriptionHtml:

We build the technology that powers billions of dollars in purchasing decisions, and we're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help lead that transformation. In this role you'll help advance procurement from individual AI-assisted productivity toward an operating model where AI increasingly supports and automates processes, with people orchestrating, verifying, and governing the work. This is a high-impact role at the intersection of technology, operations, and business strategy, where your work directly influences how Amazon procures and manages supplies at scale.

Key job responsibilities

title: Transportation Representative, NOC-NL
descriptionHtml:
TOC (Transportation Operation Center) is the central command and control center for
‘Transportation Execution’ across the Amazon Supply Chain network supporting multiple
geographies like NA, India and EU. It ensures hassle free, timely pick-up and delivery of freight
from vendors to Amazon fulfillment centers (FC) and from Amazon FCs to carrier hubs. In case
of any exceptions, TOC steps in to resolve the issue and keeps all the stakeholders informed on
the proceedings. Along with this tactical problem solving TOC is also charged with
understanding trends in network exceptions and then automating processes or proposing process
changes to streamline operations. This second aspect involves network monitoring and
significant analysis of network data.
Overall, TOC plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth functioning of Amazon transportation
and thereby has a direct impact on Amazon’s ability to serve its customers on time.
Purview of a Trans Ops Representative
A Trans Ops Representative at TOC facilitates flow of information between different
stakeholders (Trans Carriers/Hubs/Warehouses) and resolves any potential issues that impacts
customer experience and business continuity. Trans Ops Specialist at TOC works across two
verticals – Inbound and Outbound operations.
Inbound Operations deals with Vendor/Carrier/FC relationship, ensuring that the freight is
picked-up on time and is delivered at FC as per the given appointment. Trans Ops Specialist on
Inbound addresses any potential issues occurring during the lifecycle of pick-up to delivery.
Outbound Operations deals with FC/Carrier/Carrier Hub relationship, ensuring that the truck
leaves the FC in order to delivery customer orders as per promise. Trans Ops Specialist on
Outbound addresses any potential issues occurring during the lifecycle of freight leaving the FC
and reaching customer premises.
A Trans Ops Representative provides timely resolution to the issue in hand by researching and
querying internal tools and by taking real-time decisions. An ideal candidate should be able to
understand the requirements/be able to analyze data and notice trends and be able to drive
Customer Experience without compromising on time. The candidate should have the basic
understanding of Logistics and should be able to communicate clearly in the written and oral
form. Trans Ops Specialist should be able to ideate process improvements and should have the
zeal to drive them to conclusion.

Key job responsibilities
Communication with external customers (Carriers, Vendors/Suppliers) and internal customers
(Retail, Finance, Software Support, Fulfillment Centers)
· Ability to pull data from numerous databases (using Excel, Access, SQL and/or other data
management systems) and to perform ad hoc reporting and analysis as needed is a plus.
· Develop and/or understand performance metrics to assist with driving business results.
· Ability to scope out business and functional requirements for the Amazon technology teams
who create and enhance the software systems and tools are used by TOC.
· Must be able to quickly understand the business impact of the trends and make decisions that
make sense based on available data.
· Must be able to systematically escalate problems or variance in the information and data to the
relevant owners and teams and follow through on the resolutions to ensure they are delivered.
· Work within various time constraints to meet critical business needs, while measuring and
identifying activities performed.
· Excellent communication, both verbal and written as one may be required to create a narrative
outlining weekly findings and the variances to goals, and present these finding in a review
forum.
Providing real-time customer experience by working in 24*7 operating environmen

Basic qualifications

- - Experience working and communicating with multiple stakeholders, C-level executives and cross functional teams or equivalent - Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL - Experience working with fast-moving, high-performance teams and driving innovative solutions tailored to unique business environments - 10+ 2 degree

Preferred qualifications

- - Knowledge of Six Sigma, Lean manufacturing efforts, transportation and logistics, or fulfillment and distribution centers - Knowledge of and proficiency in Excel and SQL- Knowledge of Six Sigma, Lean manufacturing efforts, transportation and logistics, or fulfillment and distribution centers - Knowledge of and proficiency in Excel and SQL

title: NW Deployment Build Lead , Infra - GND
descriptionHtml:
Job description
AWS is looking for a Network Deploy Technician to join our growing team within infrastructure operations. You will work with minimum supervision in a dynamic environment to drive the stability and sustainability of our next-generation networks and assist in the development of innovative ways to automate and scale our network.

The position's responsibilities include scaling support of several data center locations and day to day assistance with capacity management. You will work closely with internal customers and external vendors to facilitate smooth project execution as directed by Network Leadership and Technical Project Managers.

You will leverage your experience supporting large scale, enterprise class networks as well as network implementation and troubleshooting. As a Network Deploy Technician, you will work in a fast paced, collaborative environment with regular peer and customer interaction. In addition to providing management and support of AWS’ vast network infrastructure, Network Deploy Technicians establish and follow best practices and refine operational procedures.

All physical requirements are expected with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 41+ pounds
• Ability to work in an environment that operates 24/7 with an ability to participate in primary responder rotation and provide after-hours support as needed
• Working in cramped and/or elevated and/or noisy environments
• Bending, lifting, stretching, reaching, standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
• Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
• Managing work and priorities through ticketing system and workflows to complete customer requests and projects
• Collaborating with various stakeholders to remove project obstacles
• Troubleshooting networking, routing and interconnectivity issues, including patch panels and patch cords
• Specifying Power and Cooling requirements and ensuring Hardware Racking/Stacking completed for new equipment
• Participating in the migration, basic configuration and rollout of new or upgraded hardware

Traveling within and outside of regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided.

A day in the life
Our team has three primary tasks:
1. Providing the first level networking devices to serve our customer racks entails various tasks (the name of the game is efficiency): You will track network rack intake and delivery; work with various onsite teams to request for rack space, power, and cooling for network racks. And then partner with network engineers to ensure all configurations are ready. You'll also be working on link and device troubleshooting within a certain Service-Level Agreement
2. There is also console builds (and room builds) that are really exciting. You'll be exposed to more teams whose goal is to provide more space and capacity for customer racks.
3. Work with ID-Scaling peers to build higher-level networking devices.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of computer hardware troubleshooting and repair experience
- 1+ years of computer networking experience
- High school or equivalent diploma

Preferred qualifications

- Experience dealing effectively with customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure

title: Area Manager II
descriptionHtml:
Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly workforce and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.
